articles.title: Malaysia Sector Outlook: Oil & Gas – No Broad Upside Despite Higher Crude Prices
articles.claim_summary: NEUTRAL view on Malaysia's oil & gas sector (KLENG Index) despite Brent crude spiking above USD115/barrel in April 2026 on the US-Iran conflict before retreating to ~USD84.4 (as of 14 Aug 2026): higher prices are not triggering a broad CAPEX upcycle, as PETRONAS's FY2026 CAPEX (~RM50bn, set pre-conflict) remains selective with no post-conflict upward revision, and Malaysia's crude output continues its structural decline (-25% since 2018, -9.4% YoY in 1Q26). Refining margins are supportive but cyclical, benefiting Petron and Hengyuan. The report favours selective stock picks -- DIALOG (recurring infrastructure income, financial resilience) and Dayang (maintenance visibility, net cash, attractive valuation) -- over broad index exposure.
